I, pp. 7 to 8), the 1887 reprint (cu31924027696404), the 1888 second edition (amielsjournaljou00amieuoft), the 1889 printings (amielsjournaljo01amiegoog, amielsjournaljou00amierich) and the 1921 Macmillan (amielsjournaljouamie00rich). Only the two A. L. Burt scans (amielsjournaljou00amieiala, amielsjournalint00amieuoft) and Gutenberg read “becomes”. So as cited to Ward 1885 the quotation carries a reprint corruption; change becomes to become and everything else in the paragraph stands verbatim in 1885. The locator is also wrong for the edition named: in the 1885 first edition (and the 1887 reprint) the entry that follows is dated 16th February 1851; it is 17th February only from the second edition (1888) on, which is what Gutenberg reproduces. Safer to anchor on the preceding entry (30th December 1850) and the page, or to cite the second edition and keep 17 February.
